full_judgment:
K. Hossain, C. J:- Bangladesh, the defendant in a suit for declaration, is the appellant before us and the matter arises out of an ex-parte decree, which the defendant attempted to set aside, but failed to get relief in the courts below. The plaintiff-respondents on the basis of annual leases from 1929 till 1950 and on payment of revenue till the acquisition of rent receiving interest on 14-4.56 claimed to have acquired tenancy right under the Government and brought the suit in 1968, for declaration of their tide. More than 254 bighas of land are involved in the suit claimed by different plaintiffs, though they have joined together to bring one suit. The suit was decreed exparte on 7-5-69, though the exparte order was recorded earlier on 7-4-69, and it was found that deficit court fees were required to be paid by the plaintiff. The Government applied for sitting aside the exparte decree and got, it set aside by an exparte order on 8-6-72, and the written statement filed by the defendant was accepted. The respondents then moved the court and got another exparte order setting aside the earlier order which set aside the exparte decree. Thereafter the application for setting aside the exparte decree was heard in presence of both sides and the trial court by its order dated 14-8-74, dismissed the Miscellaneous case by which the Government tried to set aside the exparte decree. The order was affirmed on appeal and revision. Leave was granted to consider two questions; first, whether the exparte decree passed by the trial Court satisfied the legal requirement of a judgment, and second, whether the defendant-Government made out a case for setting aside the exparte decree, in that it had sufficient cause for not appearing on the date of hearing. 

 4. If we now revert back to the order, it seems that the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of procedure in deciding the case exparte, and then giving the plaintiff an opportunity to pay the deficit court fees which he ought to have done prior to the hearing of the matter. Apart from this technical error, the trial court again committed an error of procedure in not complying with the mandatory provision. It has been only stated that P. W. 1 was examined. Exts. 1-1(d), 2-2(b) and 3-3(i) marked and the plaintiff's case proved. This does not at all satisfy the legal requirement, nor is it possible from reading the judgment that the trial court at all applied judicial mind; whether the plaintiff's witnesses and the papers produced proved the plaintiff's case. It seems that the papers reveal that a serious question of law involved is, whether the facts asserted by the plaintiffs, even if proved, confer on them their alleged tenancy right under the Government. On their own statements, they successively took yearly leases till 1950 and paid rent or revenue upto 1956. Could these facts make out a. case of tenancy right alleged by the plaintiffs? It was incumbent on the trial court to see whether such feta confer a legal title on the plaintiffs against the Government. In any event, we do not want to express any opinion on this point, excepting to say that the finding recorded by the trial Court neither satisfy the legal requirements nor from such finding the alleged case of the plaintiffs was proved. In this view of the matter, we allow the appeal with costs; set aside the judgments of the Courts below and send the case back on remand to the trial Court for disposal of the suit in accordance with law and in the light of the observations made above after hearing both the parties.
